subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe behavior should core `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error/progress reliability fix, or a documented coarse-backup boundary?
rationale: The remaining bug is concrete, but default exclusions, protected backup contents, and whether to solve this through scope control or archive reliability affect restore completeness and security, and an open closing PR already claims the implementation path.

options.title: Review or replace native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower replacement to settle smart/custom excludes, protected paths, manifest behavior, docs, and large-state proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Split reliability first
options.body: Track clear failure, progress, temp cleanup, and archive reliability here while leaving native exclude-pattern policy to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/40786.

options.title: Defer native exclusions
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document size limits and workarounds, and point optional backup strategies to plugin or ClawHub paths only if maintainers accept that boundary.

recommendation.title: Review or replace native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower replacement to settle smart/custom excludes, protected paths, manifest behavior, docs, and large-state proof before closing this issue.
